role.altitude: The production manager keeps judging permit impact, choosing improvements, leading team leaders and explaining results; collecting figures into spreadsheets, scanning government sites and tracking actions by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Reading line data critically and keeping downtime reasons coded consistently
role.ambitious_version: A manager who spends the Monday morning on the floor because the weekly report is already there.

tasks.short: Watch official publications and authority messages, check which permit requirements and conditions are affected by updates, judge the impact, and assign and track the actions.

steps.what: Production manager checks official publications and newsletters to monitor permit requirements for updates

loop.input: The week's notices from saved alerts on official publication sites, and the plant's permit conditions register.
loop.output: Each notice marked as touching or not touching the plant's activities, with the register conditions it may affect.
loop.check: The manager reads the cited article of every notice marked touching and checks that it really changes the named register condition; a mark without a citation, or where the article does not support the condition, is shown as unclear and read in full; all notices stay in the list so the manager can skim the titles of the rest.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword alerts catch the words but not whether a change applies to this plant's activities.

steps.what: Production manager reads the plant's permits to see which conditions a change touches
Production manager reads letters from the environmental agency and the industry association
Production manager judges the impact and decides what the plant must change
Production manager writes the actions with owner and due date: in a spreadsheet today, in the permit register after the change, and follows up overdue ones
Production manager checks the final actions: what each must change, the condition it serves, the owner and the due date
Production manager assigns the checked actions to their owners in the register
Action owners update the status of their own actions in the register

approvals.approved_version: The actions with what each must change, the register condition it serves, owner and due date exactly as checked by the manager in s5b, assigned once to the named owners in the permit register; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: The plant's permit conditions are kept in a register: each condition with its source, owner and due date. Saved alerts on official publication sites feed a weekly list, and a bounded step marks which notices touch the plant's activities and which register conditions they may affect, citing the article; all notices stay visible. The manager writes and checks each action and assigns it in the register; owners update their own status (s5d) and the register reminds them before due dates. Reading the agency's letters and judging impact stay with the manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes were found by reading many sites, and permit conditions sat in long PDF permits.
tasks.enabler_now: Official publication alerts, and models that mark notices against a list of conditions with citations.
tasks.still_hard: Rules whose effect depends on how the agency will interpret them.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the inspector and what they will ask about.
tasks.altitude: Less scanning; decisions on permits stay with the manager.

reach.task: Keep permits and conditions up to date
reach.learn: Whether the register shows which conditions have no owner.

evidence.claim: Language models can mark notices against a list of conditions and cite the article they rely on.
Records apps with dashboards replace compliance spreadsheets in operations.

assumptions: Boundary: from published changes to tracked actions; carrying out actions is outside.
Input contract for s1: saved alerts on official publication sites set up by the manager; industry newsletters are still read as today.

Input contract for s2: the permit conditions register, built once from the permits by the environmental and safety coordinator and kept current when permits change; s2 is priced on the register being complete.

Input contract for tracking: action owners update their status in the register themselves (s5d, share 1), with about the effort of replying to a mail. s5 keeps 55: writing actions stays, chasing owners and keeping the spreadsheet drop.
Agency letters and impact judgement keep their full time; no mechanism changes them.
unknowns: How many permits and conditions the plant has.
research_questions: Does the marked list miss changes that later matter?

already_counted.description: Production manager reads notices marked unclear and spot-checks unmarked ones.

incremental.description: Environmental and safety coordinator keeps the permit conditions register current when permits change.
Production manager tunes the saved alerts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the register is incomplete, so the manager still reads permits and s2 keeps 80, and many marks are unclear, so s1 keeps 80 (15.0); high: complete register and reliable marks as designed (28.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review cost and productivity figures, find losses with team leaders, choose improvements that are consistent with safety and environmental rules and regulations, calculate their savings and follow them up, to optimize operational costs and productivity.

steps.what: Production manager reviews cost and productivity figures: output, downtime, scrap, energy and overtime
Production manager walks the floor and discusses losses with team leaders
Production manager chooses improvements and checks they are consistent with safety and environmental rules
Production manager calculates the expected savings of the options in a spreadsheet
Production manager follows up the improvements in the weekly meeting

tasks.design: A line dashboard in the BI tool shows output, downtime by reason, scrap and energy per line and shift from the MES and the {ERP}, so the manager no longer builds the overview in a spreadsheet. A business case template takes the baseline figures from the same data. Walking the floor, choosing improvements that keep within safety and environmental rules, and follow-up stay with the manager. Figures are shown per line, not per operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures came from several systems and were combined by hand before any discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: MES and ERP data in a BI dashboard; inventory and planning tools that set targets from data.
tasks.still_hard: Trade-offs between cost, safety and the permit.
tasks.human_edge: Getting team leaders to own the improvement.
tasks.altitude: Less spreadsheet work before decisions; decisions stay with the manager.

reach.learn: Whether one dashboard ends disputes over whose figures are right.

evidence.claim: A Dutch wholesaler reports stock down over 20% with availability above 98% after configuring an inventory planning tool (vendor case).
Dashboards that show figures per worker can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: finding and following up cost and productivity improvements; running them is the team leaders' work.

Input contract for s1: machine states and counts from the MES on connected lines (about 70%) and cost postings in the {ERP}; downtime reasons coded by team leaders on the line terminal; unconnected lines come from shift reports; s1 is priced at that share.
Floor talks, choices and follow-up keep their full time.
unknowns: Which lines are connected to the MES.
research_questions: Do improvement choices change when losses are visible daily?

already_counted.description: Production manager checks odd dashboard figures with team leaders before acting.

incremental.description: Production manager agrees dashboard definitions with the controller.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many downtime reasons are left uncoded, so the manager still rebuilds part of the overview and s1 keeps 70, and the business case template is not used, so s4 keeps 100 (5.5); high: 70% of lines connected and the template used as designed (14.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Have output and downtime captured on the lines, collect production figures, calculate productivity and efficiency figures, make the tables and charts and write the commentary to prepare reports on operations.

steps.what: Team leaders record output, downtime and scrap with reasons for each shift: on a paper shift sheet today, on the line terminal after the change
Production manager collects production figures from the MES, ERP and shift reports into a spreadsheet
Production manager calculates productivity and efficiency figures: equipment effectiveness, output per hour and scrap rate
Production manager makes the tables and charts for the weekly and monthly reports
Production manager writes the commentary explaining deviations from target

loop.input: The report tables with targets, and the downtime and scrap reasons coded by team leaders.
loop.output: A draft list of the largest deviations against target with their figures and coded reasons.
loop.check: The manager checks that each listed deviation is one of the largest in the tables and that its coded reason fits what happened on the line; every figure must match the report tables and every reason must be a coded reason in the data, or the line is marked; the manager writes the causes and actions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables show all deviations; the reader needs the few that matter in words.

tasks.design: On connected lines the MES counts output and machine states itself, and team leaders tap downtime and scrap reasons on the line terminal instead of writing a shift sheet. The report pulls these figures and cost postings from the {ERP}, computes equipment effectiveness, output per hour and scrap with fixed formulas, and fills the weekly and monthly tables and charts. A bounded step drafts the list of largest deviations with figures and coded reasons; the manager writes causes and actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures were copied from shift sheets and several systems into a spreadsheet each week.
tasks.enabler_now: MES line data, BI report templates and models that draft text checked against tables.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining why a line underperformed when the codes do not tell.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which deviation the director will ask about.
tasks.altitude: Most report building goes; interpretation stays with the manager.

reach.learn: Whether coding reasons on the terminal is as quick as the paper sheet.

evidence.claim: MES and BI tools compute equipment effectiveness from machine states and counts.
Shift data per team member can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from shift data to the written report; presenting it is outside.

Input contract for s2: machine states and counts from the MES on connected lines (about 70% of output), downtime and scrap reasons tapped by team leaders on the line terminal (s1) with about the effort of the paper sheet, cost postings from the {ERP}; unconnected lines are typed from shift sheets; s2 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s3 and s4: the production data from s2; formulas and templates set up once by the manager with the controller.
Team leaders' time is outside the manager's savings.
unknowns: How many reports the manager prepares per month.
research_questions: Do reports come out earlier and with fewer corrections?

already_counted.description: Production manager checks figures for unconnected lines and odd values.
Production manager edits the drafted deviation list.

incremental.description: Production manager maintains report formulas and the downtime reason list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only about half of output comes from connected lines, so s2 keeps 60 and checking computed figures keeps s3 at 50 (42.0); high: about 70% of output connected as designed (54.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hold the daily start meeting, coach and give feedback, handle leave, swap and overtime requests, hold absence talks and prepare appraisal forms to supervise subordinate employees.

steps.what: Production manager holds the daily start meeting with team leaders
Production manager supervises subordinate employees: coaches, gives feedback and holds performance talks
Employees ask for leave, shift swaps or overtime: on a paper form or by phone today, in the self-service app after the change
Production manager handles leave, swap and overtime requests against staffing
Production manager holds absence and return-to-work talks
Production manager prepares the appraisal forms for team leaders

tasks.design: Employees ask for leave, swaps and overtime in the {HCM} self-service app, which checks the requests against staffing minimums per shift and the CAO rules, and the manager approves or refuses in the app. Appraisal forms open with last year's goals and agreements already filled in. Meetings, coaching, absence talks and the appraisal itself stay with the manager; no system scores staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came on paper and by phone and were checked against a roster spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: HR self-service apps with staffing rules.
tasks.still_hard: Saying no to a swap that matters to the employee.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a team leader is overloaded before they say so.
tasks.altitude: Less paperwork around staffing; leadership does not change.

reach.task: Support managers on absence and appraisal
reach.learn: Whether prefilled forms make appraisals more consistent.

evidence.claim: A Danish study of 25,000 workers found chatbots saved 2.8% of hours, with earnings and hours unchanged.
Systems for appraisal and staff monitoring need works council consent.
AI that allocates work or scores staff performance is an AI Act high-risk use; the design uses none.

assumptions: Boundary: day-to-day supervision; hiring and pay are separate tasks.

Input contract for s4: requests entered by employees in the self-service app (s3) with about the effort of a paper form; staffing minimums and CAO rules set by HR; about 80% of requests go through the app.
Meetings, coaching and absence talks keep their full time; employee time is outside the manager's savings.
research_questions: Do employees get faster answers on swaps?

already_counted.description: Production manager decides requests the rules flag as conflicts.

incremental.description: Production manager checks staffing minimums in the app each season.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only about half of requests go through the app, so s4 keeps 80 (7.0); high: about 80% of requests through the app as designed (11.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
